title: Will Brazil pick the U.S. or China?
gist: Video page in which Adam Tooze asks whether Brazil will align with the U.S. or China; the captured text contains no transcript, only the headline and related FP coverage of Brazil's 2026 election, including Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy and the view that slow growth and corruption persist regardless of who wins.

themes.theme: Brazil between the U.S. and China

insights.claim: Adam Tooze frames Brazil as facing a strategic choice between aligning with the United States or China, in an October 2026 Foreign Policy video.
insights.speaker: Adam Tooze
insights.so_what: Brazil's alignment affects commodity trade flows, Chinese investment and U.S. tariff exposure for a major EM economy.
insights.locator: Will Brazil pick the U.S. or China?

insights.claim: Related Foreign Policy coverage argues Brazil's election will not fix its biggest problems because slow growth and corruption have dogged both the right and the left.
insights.speaker: Adam Tooze
insights.so_what: Neither electoral outcome is likely to shift Brazil's structural growth outlook.
insights.quote: Slow growth and corruption have dogged the right and the left.
insights.locator: Brazil’s Election Won’t Fix Its Biggest Problems

insights.claim: Flávio Bolsonaro is a presidential candidate in Brazil's 2026 election while President Lula is betting big on defense ahead of the vote.
insights.speaker: Adam Tooze
insights.so_what: The election pits the Bolsonaro dynasty against Lula, with geopolitical alignment at stake.
